creator: Alexander Terp
description:
The wheel is already safe and already right: terminal.scroll is structured, and the daemon encodes it against the pane's real state (wheel_routing, encode_mouse_wheel, alternate scroll, or its own scrollback). Muster sends scroll intents and gets correct behavior knowing nothing.

Buttons and motion have no equivalent command. Encoding them client-side means writing SGR sequences into the PTY blind, and a program that never enabled mouse reporting receives them as typed text - garbage in a shell, a corrupted prompt in an agent. A mis-encoded key is a wrong key; a mis-sent click is injected input.

So this waits on the mode exposure tracked in a_27CTRluw7. When InputState is readable, mouse_protocol_mode and mouse_protocol_encoding say both whether to send and which encoding to use, and the encoder itself comes from libghostty-vt's mouse/encoder.h rather than being hand-rolled.

Staging: the mode profile seam in the core is where this switches on, so the work is a flag plus an encoder, not a redesign.
title: Mouse buttons and motion: blocked on pane mode exposure
